thread:
kevin_customer: hey team, installing the private agent in a customer VPC. model pulls fail during startup — TLS handshake / 403 from our model registry and auth calls. installer stops with 'download failed'. can you share the egress hosts/ports we need to allow?

maria_support: thanks — can you paste the exact curl output from the node where the installer runs? also which installer variant (k8s helm / airgap / unattended)?

kevin_customer: helm chart on EKS (private subnets). here's quick repro from a node:
```
curl -v https://model-registry.redwood-inference.internal/shards/abc123 -o /dev/null
*   Trying 10.10.20.5...
* Connected to model-registry.redwood-inference.internal (10.10.20.5) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
* server certificate: CN=proxy.local
* SSL: certificate subject name (proxy.local) does not match target host name 'model-registry.redwood-inference.internal'
* Closing connection 0
curl: (51) SSL: certificate subject name (proxy.local) does not match target host name 'model-registry.redwood-inference.internal'
```
so looks like a TLS MITM (corporate proxy) returning its cert. also seeing 403 from auth endpoint when the agent tries service-to-service auth.

sasha_engr: yep, smells like TLS intercept / split-horizon DNS. two quick checks:
1) from the same node run: `openssl s_client -connect model-registry.redwood-inference.internal:443 -servername model-registry.redwood-inference.internal` and paste the cert chain.
2) `dig +short model-registry.redwood-inference.internal` (are you resolving to a private IP?)
if the cert CN is a proxy or the chain ends in your corp CA, TLS inspection is interfering — you need the proxy to preserve SNI or skip TLS inspection for our hosts.

maria_support: to unblock, can you temporarily set the installer env var to disable telemetry/auth calls so at least the agent can start? use `REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=true` and `REDWOOD_AUTH_BYPASS=true` for a repro test only — we'll need those hosts allowed long-term.

rajeev_infra: listing the endpoints we require (short form) — allow TCP 443 outbound to:
- model-registry.api.redwood-inference.com
- auth.api.redwood-inference.com
- telemetry.ingest.redwood-inference.com
- packages.redwood-inference.com (package index / wheels)
- registry-1.docker.io (docker pulls)
- ghcr.io and api.github.com (image & webhook calls)
- *.s3.amazonaws.com (model shard storage)
- cdn.fastly.net / artifacts.global.fastly.net (shard CDN)
- pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org (pip wheels)
Notes: allow SNI passthrough (no TLS MITM) or install your corp CA into the node trust store so canonical certs validate. also allow outbound to OCSP/CRL endpoints used by your CA (e.g., ocsp.digicert.com) if TLS stapling/OCSP checks are enforced.

kevin_customer: helpful, thanks. any specific headers/ips? customer runs NAT egress through a small pool of IPs — can we get IP ranges?

rajeev_infra: we don't publish fixed IPs for the hosted model store (varies by region). recommended patterns:
- allow by FQDN + SNI (preferred)
- if you must allow IPs, permit the cloud provider S3 CDN / Fastly ranges for your region (we can share a short list after region is confirmed).
Also disable TLS interception for the FQDNs above — we've seen many failures where proxies rewrite certs and drop SNI, resulting in 403/401 from our auth edge.

deploybot: automated note — installer telemetry attempts to https://telemetry.ingest.redwood-inference.com once every 30s during bootstrap, and model registry auth at https://auth.api.redwood-inference.com/token.

maria_support: quick workaround steps for now:
- allow SNI passthrough / bypass TLS inspect for the listed hosts
- add no_proxy for the installer pod with the hostnames (e.g., NO_PROXY=model-registry.redwood-inference.internal,auth.api.redwood-inference.com)
- if you can't change proxy, install the corp CA on nodes so the agent trusts the proxy cert (less ideal)

kevin_customer: will test SSL passthrough & add the FQDNs to the no_proxy. i'll report back in ~30m. thanks :thumbsup:

kevin_customer (later): confirming — after bypassing TLS inspect for model-registry.* and allowing outbound to *.s3.amazonaws.com the agent completed startup and model pulls succeeded. auth and telemetry now pass.
maria_support: great — we'll follow up with a short KB and a region-specific IP list if they need IP-based firewall rules. closing the case once you confirm with the customer. :white_check_mark:
